intro: The Box Shadow Generator builds a CSS box-shadow value from horizontal and vertical offsets, blur, spread, and a color, with a live preview so you can see the result as you adjust it. It outputs a ready-to-paste box-shadow declaration and supports an inset toggle, making it handy for quickly dialing in shadows for cards, buttons, and other UI elements.
useCases: Designing drop shadows for cards, modals, and dropdown menus
Creating inset shadows for input fields or pressed-button states
Tweaking offset, blur, and spread values visually instead of guessing in code
Generating a box-shadow declaration to paste straight into a stylesheet or component
Experimenting with subtle vs. heavy shadows using an rgba color with adjustable opacity

faq.q: Is my data sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The generator runs entirely in your browser and nothing is uploaded. All values and the preview are computed client-side.

faq.q: What units do the X, Y, blur, and spread fields use?
faq.a: They are treated as pixel values; the generator appends px to whatever number you enter. So entering 4 for Y produces 4px in the output.

faq.q: What color formats can I use?
faq.a: The color field is free text, so you can enter any valid CSS color such as an rgba() value, a hex code, or a named color. The default is rgba(0,0,0,0.25).
Yes. Toggling the inset option prefixes the value with the inset keyword, producing an inner shadow instead of an outer one.

faq.q: Can I create multiple stacked shadows at once?
faq.a: The tool generates a single box-shadow value. To stack multiple shadows, you can generate each one and combine them in your CSS, separated by commas.
